2609.22695.title: A Survey on the Linear Representation Hypothesis
2609.22695.paper_summary: The term "linear representation hypothesis" (LRH) has appeared across diverse subfields of artificial intelligence, neuroscience, and cognitive science. But previous works have not consistently treated the LRH as a falsifiable scientific hypothesis; we analyze these inconsistencies and examine their implications for how prior theoretical and methodological results should be interpreted. Based on this analysis, we argue that claims regarding linear representations become well-defined only through careful examination of the model, representation location, feature definition, and evaluation dataset. We therefore propose a more rigorous formalization of the LRH that makes these dependencies explicit and allows the hypothesis to be evaluated as a falsifiable scientific claim. Finally, we identify some non-trivial open problems that warrant further attention from the research community.
2609.22695.paper_summary_zh: “線性表徵假說”（LRH）這個術語已出現在人工智慧、神經科學和認知科學的多個子領域中。<lb/>但以往的研究並未一致地將LRH視為可證偽的科學假說；我們分析這些不一致之處並檢視其對於如何解釋先前理論和方法論結果的影響。<lb/>基於這一分析，我們主張有關線性表徵的主張只有通過對模型、表徵位置、特徵定義和評估數據集的仔細檢查才能明確定義。<lb/>因此，我們提出了一種更嚴謹的LRH形式化，使這些依賴關係變得明確，並允許該假說作為可證偽的科學主張進行評估。<lb/>最後，我們確定了一些值得研究社群進一步關注的非平凡開放問題。
